title: SC07 lifecycle-event-ledger.schema.json -- append-only ledger row (05-DATA-MODEL.md §2 row lifecycle_event + §4 M1 columns + record_locator)
description: One row per batch operation, appended, never rewritten and never deleted by the write path. `detail` is explicitly not a source of truth (05 §2 row 8; CM-66 15 decision_rules: audit detail 不作为事实来源, stated in the code comment). Columns are exactly 05 §4 M1's merged ledger: {at, op, actor, reason, supersedes, superseded_by, entity, entity_id} plus the kernel's content_hash binding, this file's record_locator projection, and `seq`.

seq.description: Additive mechanism field, not policy: the row's 1-based position, which is what makes 'append-only' checkable -- S12/recover compares ledger length against the store/_ledger/commit.json commit marker and reports drift instead of repairing it. No YAML parameter in .distill/round-3/DEFERRED-PARAMETERS.yaml covers it (registered in W1-C-REPORT.md).

at.description: Captured once by the writer and reused for every row of the batch (05 §2: 时间戳取一次).

op.description: 07 §2: the original 8 policy actions, plus the user-approved 2026-10-07 RESTORE inverse of committed knowledge through S12. RESTORE is not crash recovery, automatic resurrection or a new storage state. MOVE/AUTOMATE remain restricted UPDATE/ARCHIVE cases. DELETE is still unreachable through S12.

actor.description: 05 §4 M1: DD-4 {curator, user, merge, agent} union Agent 12 {human, import, shared}. actor/reason are written as a pair, so a move is attributable to a owner or to automation.

reason.description: 05 §4 M1 closed enum. null is legal because Round 2 adjudicated reasons for the archive/merge/decay family only; ADD / UPDATE / SUPERSEDE / REINFORCE have no adjudicated value and S12 writes null rather than inventing one (IMPLEMENTATION_GAP in W1-C-REPORT.md). M4 additionally requires the origin of a tombstone to be recorded here, rejecting 15's 'two ticket sources deliberately indistinguishable'.

entity.description: 05 §1: the five entities and their boundaries.

supersedes.description: 05 §4 M4: the supersession pair, kept strictly separate from the reversible tombstone ticket -- SUPERSEDE and DELETE must never share a state bit.

detail.description: Human-readable only. NEVER authoritative: a consumer that reads `detail` instead of the columns above re-creates the RT-09 shape (a claim in prose with no writer behind it).

record_locator.description: Self-describing pointer, per 05 §2 row 10: the authoritative provenance trail is held by the ledger owner, and an artifact body carries only this reference.

seq.description: Must equal this row's own seq; a mismatch means the row was copied out of band.

content_hash.description: Written by kd_provenance.append_ledger over the canonical row. It is what makes an in-place edit of an appended row detectable, since an append-only file offers no other hook.

ledger_invariants.description: Not expressible in a single JSON Schema pass over one row; enforced by kd_write_txn + the integrator's re-run:
invariants: append-only: existing bytes are never rewritten; a row whose seq is not file position is a defect, and deletion-eligibility is a revocable state bit (tombstoned_at), never a ledger action taken here
one row per batch op: a batch of N intents appends N rows and never a second row for the same op

sweeping the ledger by byte cap MUST warn loudly -- 05 §2 row 8 records 14's ledger_max_bytes=5MiB as a registered risk of destroying audit evidence; S12 currently performs no sweep and no cap value was adjudicated
rejected proposals stay visible: a refused batch writes nothing and surfaces a non-zero exit code rather than an empty success
